lecons.titre: Greetings at Different Times of Day, Sight Words, and Auxiliary Verbs
savoirs_faire: Greet people and respond appropriately to greetings given in the morning, afternoon, and night
Read sight words correctly and copy short texts of at least five sentences legibly
Use auxiliary verbs (is, are, was, do, does) appropriately in simple sentences

exercices.enonce: Bella and Mballa practice this in Douala (Week 1, Page 4): Greetings at Different Times of Day, Sight Words, and Auxiliary Verbs.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: What is the correct greeting to use in the morning?
quiz.explication: 'Good morning' is used to greet people early in the day.

quiz.question: Which word is an auxiliary verb?
quiz.explication: 'Is' is an auxiliary verb used to form other verb tenses.

quiz.question: What should you do when someone greets you politely?
quiz.explication: It is polite to respond appropriately when greeted.

lecons.contenu:
Greetings at Different Times of Day, Sight Words, and Auxiliary Verbs

What you will learn:

  • Greet people and respond appropriately to greetings given in the morning, afternoon, and night
  • Read sight words correctly and copy short texts of at least five sentences legibly
  • Use auxiliary verbs (is, are, was, do, does) appropriately in simple sentences

lecons.titre: Songs, Multisyllabic Words, and Kinds of Nouns (Common, Proper, Concrete)
savoirs_faire: Sing songs using correct tones and melody, and read short texts audibly
Write sentences with apostrophes correctly (spelling and dictation)
Identify and use common, proper, and concrete nouns in simple sentences

exercices.enonce: Bella and Mballa practice this in Douala (Week 2, Page 5): Songs, Multisyllabic Words, and Kinds of Nouns.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: Which of these is a proper noun?
quiz.explication: Douala is the name of a specific place, so it is a proper noun.

quiz.question: Which word uses an apostrophe correctly?
quiz.explication: The apostrophe shows that the book belongs to Bella.

quiz.question: A concrete noun names something you can:
quiz.explication: Concrete nouns name things that can be touched, seen, or felt.

lecons.contenu:
Songs, Multisyllabic Words, and Kinds of Nouns (Common, Proper, Concrete)

What you will learn:

  • Sing songs using correct tones and melody, and read short texts audibly
  • Write sentences with apostrophes correctly (spelling and dictation)
  • Identify and use common, proper, and concrete nouns in simple sentences

In Douala (Week 2, Page 5), Bella and Mballa practice: songs, multisyllabic words, and kinds of nouns!

lecons.titre: Traditional Songs, Words with Apostrophe S, and Adventure Stories
savoirs_faire: Sing popular traditional songs using correct tones and melody, and show love for reading
Write sentences with apostrophe s' correctly and identify nouns in simple sentences
Read adventure stories with short texts and deduce simple lessons from them

exercices.enonce: Bella and Mballa practice this in Douala (Week 3, Page 5): Traditional Songs, Words with Apostrophe S, and Adventure Stories.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: What kind of story did Bella read this week?
quiz.explication: Bella read an adventure story with short texts.

quiz.question: Which sentence uses apostrophe s' correctly?
quiz.explication: Apostrophe s' shows possession: the ball belongs to the boy.

quiz.question: Traditional songs in Cameroon are usually sung:
quiz.explication: Traditional songs are sung using correct tones and melody.

lecons.contenu:
Traditional Songs, Words with Apostrophe S, and Adventure Stories

What you will learn:

  • Sing popular traditional songs using correct tones and melody, and show love for reading
  • Write sentences with apostrophe s' correctly and identify nouns in simple sentences
  • Read adventure stories with short texts and deduce simple lessons from them

In Douala (Week 3, Page 5), Bella and Mballa practice: traditional songs, words with apostrophe s, and adventure stories!

lecons.titre: Counting to 100, Set Symbols, Days of the Week, 3D Shapes, and Data Collection
savoirs_faire: Count numbers up to 100
Distinguish between different set symbols
Name the days of the week, identify and draw 3-dimensional shapes, and collect data on a given topic

exercices.enonce: Manyi and Ashu practise this in Buea (Week 1, Page 22): Counting to 100, Set Symbols, Days of the Week, 3D Shapes, and Data Collection.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: Counting up to 100 mainly practises a pupil's skill in:
quiz.explication: Counting numbers is part of the Numbers and Operations domain.

quiz.question: A 3-dimensional shape has:
quiz.explication: 3D (3-dimensional) shapes have length, width, and height.

quiz.question: Collecting data on a topic helps pupils to:
quiz.explication: Collecting data is the first step of statistics and graph work.

lecons.contenu:
Counting to 100, Set Symbols, Days of the Week, 3D Shapes, and Data Collection

What you will learn:

  • Count numbers up to 100
  • Distinguish between different set symbols
  • Name the days of the week, identify and draw 3-dimensional shapes, and collect data on a given topic

In Buea (Week 1, Page 22), Manyi and Ashu practise: counting to 100, set symbols, days of the week, 3d shapes, and data collection!

lecons.titre: Writing Numbers to 100, Elements of a Set, Months of the Year & Lunar Months, and 4D Shapes
savoirs_faire: Write numbers up to 100 in figures
Identify the elements of a set
Name the months of the year and describe the 13 lunar months, and construct 4-dimensional shapes

exercices.enonce: Tabe and Njoh practise this in Kumba (Week 2, Page 22): Writing Numbers to 100, Elements of a Set, Months of the Year & Lunar Months, and 4D Shapes.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: Writing numbers up to 100 is part of which domain?
quiz.explication: Writing numbers is part of the Numbers and Operations domain.

quiz.question: The elements of a set are:
options: The individual members that belong to the set
quiz.explication: Elements are the individual members that make up a set.

quiz.question: The Gregorian calendar year has how many months?
quiz.explication: The Gregorian calendar has 12 months, alongside the 13 traditional lunar months studied.

lecons.contenu:
Writing Numbers to 100, Elements of a Set, Months of the Year & Lunar Months, and 4D Shapes

What you will learn:

  • Write numbers up to 100 in figures
  • Identify the elements of a set
  • Name the months of the year and describe the 13 lunar months, and construct 4-dimensional shapes

In Kumba (Week 2, Page 22), Tabe and Njoh practise: writing numbers to 100, elements of a set, months of the year & lunar months, and 4d shapes!

lecons.titre: Counting 101-500, Equal & Equivalent Sets, Ordinary vs. Leap Year, and Ascending Order Ranking
savoirs_faire: Count and write numbers from 101 to 500
Differentiate between equal sets and equivalent sets
Distinguish an ordinary year from a leap year, and arrange numbers in ascending order

exercices.enonce: Besong and Enow practise this in Limbe (Week 3, Page 23): Counting 101-500, Equal & Equivalent Sets, Ordinary vs. Leap Year, and Ascending Order Ranking.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: Two sets are equal when they have:
options: The same number of elements only
quiz.explication: Equal sets have exactly the same elements, while equivalent sets only have the same number of elements.

quiz.question: A leap year has how many days in February?
quiz.explication: A leap year has 29 days in February instead of the usual 28.

quiz.question: Arranging numbers in ascending order means arranging them:
quiz.explication: Ascending order means arranging numbers from the smallest to the biggest.

lecons.contenu:
Counting 101-500, Equal & Equivalent Sets, Ordinary vs. Leap Year, and Ascending Order Ranking

What you will learn:

  • Count and write numbers from 101 to 500
  • Differentiate between equal sets and equivalent sets
  • Distinguish an ordinary year from a leap year, and arrange numbers in ascending order

In Limbe (Week 3, Page 23), Besong and Enow practise: counting 101-500, equal & equivalent sets, ordinary vs. leap year, and ascending order ranking!

lecons.titre: The Number Line to 20, Descending Order Ranking, and Integration & Remediation
savoirs_faire: Locate points on a number line up to 20
Arrange numbers in descending order
Use knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired this ILT to solve daily-life mathematical problems

exercices.enonce: Mbah and Achu practise this in Bamenda (Week 4, Page 23): The Number Line to 20, Descending Order Ranking, and Integration & Remediation.
exercices.astuce: Remember to read the page carefully and practice with your own examples.

quiz.question: A number line up to 20 shows numbers from:
quiz.explication: A number line up to 20 shows the numbers 0 to 20 placed in order.

quiz.question: Arranging numbers in descending order means arranging them:
quiz.explication: Descending order means arranging numbers from the biggest to the smallest.

quiz.question: This week's activity mainly helps pupils to:
options: Apply this ILT's knowledge to daily-life problems
quiz.explication: Integration weeks apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired to real situations.

lecons.contenu:
The Number Line to 20, Descending Order Ranking, and Integration & Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Locate points on a number line up to 20
  • Arrange numbers in descending order
  • Use knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired this ILT to solve daily-life mathematical problems

In Bamenda (Week 4, Page 23), Mbah and Achu practise: the number line to 20, descending order ranking, and integration & remediation!

lecons.titre: Body Parts, Local Tools (Carpenter/Farming/Hunting), and Home Components
savoirs_faire: Identify and name main external parts of the human body (head, eyes, ears, hands, legs)
Identify and list common tools used in the locality by carpenters, farmers, and hunters
Identify and name components of the immediate home environment (sitting room, kitchen, bedroom, yard)

exercices.enonce: Tanyi identifies body parts and tools in Douala: Hands (body part); Hoe and Cutlass (farming tools); Sitting room (home component).
exercices.astuce: Body parts allow us to move and work; tools help farmers and carpenters perform tasks in the home.

quiz.question: Which body part is used for seeing objects in our environment?
quiz.explication: Eyes are the organs of sight.

quiz.question: Which tool is commonly used by farmers in Cameroonian villages to clear bushes?
quiz.explication: Cutlasses are farming tools for clearing bushes.

quiz.question: Which area is a component of the immediate home environment?
quiz.explication: Kitchen and sitting room are home components.

quiz.question: Which tool is used by carpenters to drive nails into wood?
quiz.explication: Hammers are carpentry tools.

lecons.contenu:
Body Parts, Local Tools (Carpenter/Farming/Hunting), and Home Components

What you will learn:

  • Identify and name main external parts of the human body (head, eyes, ears, hands, legs)
  • Identify and list common tools used in the locality by carpenters, farmers, and hunters
  • Identify and name components of the immediate home environment (sitting room, kitchen, bedroom, yard)

In Douala (Week 1, Page 33), Tanyi identifies external body parts, names local farming/carpentry tools (cutlass, hammer), and lists home components!

lecons.titre: Body Care, Uses of Local Tools, and School Components
savoirs_faire: Discuss and demonstrate effective ways to care for human body parts (washing hands, bathing)
Describe practical uses of local tools in carpentry, farming, and hunting
Identify and name physical components of the school environment (classrooms, office, playground, latrines)

exercices.enonce: Ngo Mbog practices body care in Douala: Wash hands with soap and water before meals. School components: classrooms, playground.
exercices.astuce: Taking care of body parts prevents diseases; school components provide safe learning spaces.

quiz.question: Why is it necessary to wash hands with clean water and soap regularly?
options: To remove germs and prevent disease
quiz.explication: Washing hands removes harmful germs.

quiz.question: Which school component is designed for pupils to play during recreation break?
quiz.explication: Playgrounds are for recreation break.

quiz.question: What is the practical use of a hoe in farming?
quiz.explication: Hoes till soil and make ridges.

quiz.question: Which action cares for body teeth?
quiz.explication: Brushing twice daily keeps teeth healthy.

lecons.contenu:
Body Care, Uses of Local Tools, and School Components

What you will learn:

  • Discuss and demonstrate effective ways to care for human body parts (washing hands, bathing)
  • Describe practical uses of local tools in carpentry, farming, and hunting
  • Identify and name physical components of the school environment (classrooms, office, playground, latrines)

In Douala (Week 2, Page 33), Ngo Mbog discusses body hygiene habits, names uses of farming tools, and identifies school components!

lecons.titre: Advanced Body Hygiene, Demonstration of Tools, and Community Places
savoirs_faire: Explain advanced personal hygiene routines for body hygiene (trimming nails, cleaning ears safely)
Demonstrate safe handling and operation of different local tools
Locate and name essential public places in the local community (health center, market, water tap, police post)

exercices.enonce: Bikoy demonstrates tool handling in Douala: Hold cutlass handle firmly away from body. Community places: Health center, Market.
exercices.astuce: Always handle sharp tools with caution; community places provide public health and essential services.

quiz.question: Which hygiene practice prevents dirt from hiding under fingernails?
quiz.explication: Trimming nails short stops dirt accumulation.

quiz.question: Which public place in the community provides medical treatments for sick people?
quiz.explication: Health Centers provide medical treatment.

quiz.question: How should sharp farming tools like cutlasses be carried safely?
options: By the wooden handle pointing downwards
quiz.explication: Tools should be carried safely by the handle.

quiz.question: Which community place supplies clean drinking water for families?
quiz.explication: Standpipes and boreholes supply clean water.

lecons.contenu:
Advanced Body Hygiene, Demonstration of Tools, and Community Places

What you will learn:

  • Explain advanced personal hygiene routines for body hygiene (trimming nails, cleaning ears safely)
  • Demonstrate safe handling and operation of different local tools
  • Locate and name essential public places in the local community (health center, market, water tap, police post)

In Douala (Week 3, Page 34), Bikoy practices nail trimming hygiene, demonstrates safe tool handling, and locates community places!

lecons.titre: Local Machines (Sewing/Grinding) and Community Integration
savoirs_faire: Identify and classify types of simple machines found in the locality (sewing machine, cassava grinding mill, bicycle)
Describe how simple machines make work easier in daily community life
Locate community services and apply Health, Tech, and Environmental knowledge to daily life scenarios
Complete September Science & Technology integration and assessment

exercices.enonce: Ekwalla visits the grinding mill in Douala: Grinding machine grinds maize quickly. Sewing machine sews clothes. Machines make work easier.
exercices.astuce: Machines reduce human effort and speed up work in our locality.

quiz.question: Which machine in the locality grinds cassava and maize into flour?
quiz.explication: Grinding mills process cassava and grains.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of using simple machines in daily work?
options: They make work faster and easier
quiz.explication: Machines reduce effort and speed work.

quiz.question: Which machine is used by tailors to stitch clothes together?
quiz.explication: Sewing machines stitch fabrics.

quiz.question: Which simple transport machine uses pedals to move people around the village?
quiz.explication: Bicycles use foot pedals for transport.

lecons.contenu:
Local Machines (Sewing/Grinding) and Community Integration

What you will learn:

  • Identify and classify types of simple machines found in the locality (sewing machine, cassava grinding mill, bicycle)
  • Describe how simple machines make work easier in daily community life
  • Locate community services and apply Health, Tech, and Environmental knowledge to daily life scenarios
  • Complete September Science & Technology integration and assessment

In Douala (Week 4, Page 34), Ekwalla identifies local machines (grinding mill, sewing machine), explains their work benefits, and completes September ST!

lecons.titre: Salutations (bonjour, salut, bonsoir), lexique du salon, le nom et le groupe nominal
savoirs_faire: Saluer et se présenter oralement (bonjour, salut, bonsoir)
Lire des mots et de courtes phrases relatifs au centre d'intérêt La Maison, contexte le salon
Identifier le nom (avec ses déterminants) et le groupe nominal dans une phrase, utiliser le dictionnaire bilingue

exercices.enonce: Mballa entre au salon à Yaoundé et dit : 'Bonjour Maman !' Le groupe nominal : 'le salon'.
exercices.astuce: Le groupe nominal est formé d'un nom et de son déterminant, ex. le salon, la table.

quiz.question: Quelle salutation utilise-t-on le matin en entrant au salon ?
quiz.explication: 'Bonjour' se dit le matin.

quiz.question: Dans 'le salon', quel est le déterminant ?
quiz.explication: 'le' est le déterminant du nom 'salon'.

quiz.question: Que contient un groupe nominal ?
quiz.explication: Le groupe nominal associe déterminant et nom.

lecons.contenu:
Salutations (bonjour, salut, bonsoir), lexique du salon, le nom et le groupe nominal

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Saluer et se présenter oralement (bonjour, salut, bonsoir)
  • Lire des mots et phrases du salon
  • Identifier le nom et le groupe nominal, utiliser le dictionnaire bilingue

À Yaoundé (Semaine 1, Page 42), Mballa salue sa famille dans le salon, apprend le vocabulaire de la maison et découvre le groupe nominal !

lecons.titre: Salutations selon le moment (bonne après-midi, comment allez-vous), types de noms, cédille et deux-points
savoirs_faire: Saluer selon le moment de la journée (bonne après-midi, bonne nuit, comment allez-vous, comment ça va)
Reconnaître les types de noms (nom commun, nom propre) dans une phrase relative à la cuisine
Orthographier des mots avec la cédille (ç) et utiliser les deux-points (:)

exercices.enonce: Dans la cuisine à Yaoundé, Mballa demande : 'Bonne après-midi Maman, comment allez-vous ?' Elle répond : 'Je vais bien, garçon !' (cédille : garçon)
exercices.astuce: La cédille sous le 'c' (ç) donne le son 's' devant a, o, u, comme dans garçon.

quiz.question: Que dit-on le soir avant de se coucher ?
quiz.explication: 'Bonne nuit' se dit avant de dormir.

quiz.question: Lequel de ces mots prend une cédille ?
quiz.explication: 'Garçon' s'écrit avec ç.

quiz.question: Quel signe introduit une énumération ?
quiz.explication: Les deux-points annoncent une liste ou une explication.

lecons.contenu:
Salutations selon le moment, types de noms, cédille et deux-points

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Saluer selon le moment de la journée
  • Reconnaître les types de noms
  • Utiliser la cédille et les deux-points

À Yaoundé (Semaine 2, Page 43), Mballa aide en cuisine, apprend à saluer à tout moment de la journée et découvre la cédille !

lecons.titre: Se présenter, adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs, apostrophe, et évaluation de septembre
savoirs_faire: Se présenter et présenter quelqu'un (je m'appelle..., il/elle s'appelle..., j'habite à...)
Utiliser les adjectifs possessifs et les adjectifs démonstratifs
Employer l'apostrophe, le point d'interrogation et le point d'exclamation ; réviser la météo et les objets de la concession pour l'évaluation de fin septembre

exercices.enonce: Aux toilettes de la concession à Yaoundé, Mballa dit : 'Je m'appelle Mballa, j'habite à Yaoundé. Cette porte est fermée !'
exercices.astuce: L'apostrophe (l') remplace 'le' ou 'la' devant une voyelle, comme dans j'habite.

quiz.question: Comment se présente-t-on en français ?
quiz.explication: 'Je m'appelle...' sert à se présenter.

quiz.question: 'Cette porte' contient quel type de mot ?
quiz.explication: 'Cette' est un adjectif démonstratif.

quiz.question: Quel temps fait-il si on dit 'il pleut' ?
quiz.explication: 'Il pleut' décrit un temps pluvieux, vu en révision de septembre.

lecons.contenu:
Se présenter, adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs, apostrophe, et évaluation de septembre

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Se présenter et présenter quelqu'un
  • Utiliser les adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs
  • Employer l'apostrophe et réviser septembre (météo, objets de la concession)

À Yaoundé (Semaines 3-4, Pages 44-45), Mballa se présente, utilise les adjectifs possessifs et démonstratifs, parle du temps qu'il fait, et révise tout le mois de septembre !

lecons.titre: Definition & Types of History, Definition of Geography, National Flag, and Greeting Etiquettes
savoirs_faire: Define History (the study of past events) and name types of history (family history, local history, national history)
Define Geography (the study of the Earth, its features, and human interaction) and state reasons for studying it
Explain the four National Emblems (focusing on the Flag) and practice simple greeting etiquettes

exercices.enonce: Fotso defines history in Bafoussam: 'History is the study of past events.' Geography studies Earth's mountains and rivers.
exercices.astuce: History studies the past; Geography studies the Earth and environment.

quiz.question: What is the definition of History in Social Studies?
options: The study of past events, people, and places
quiz.explication: History is the study of past events.

quiz.question: What subject studies the Earth's physical features like mountains, rivers, and climate?
quiz.explication: Geography studies physical Earth features.

quiz.question: What greeting etiquette shows respect when meeting elders in Bafoussam?
options: Greeting politely with a clear voice and respectful posture
quiz.explication: Polite greetings show respect to elders.

lecons.contenu:
Definition & Types of History, Definition of Geography, National Flag, and Greeting Etiquettes

What you will learn:

  • Define History (the study of past events) and name types of history (family history, local history, national history)
  • Define Geography (the study of the Earth, its features, and human interaction) and state reasons for studying it
  • Explain the four National Emblems (focusing on the Flag) and practice simple greeting etiquettes

In Bafoussam (Week 1, Page 67), Fotso defines history and geography, names types of history, explains national emblems (flag), and practices greeting etiquettes!

lecons.titre: Sources of History (Newspapers & Magazines), Physical Features (Mountains in Cameroon), National Anthem, and Apologies
savoirs_faire: Describe printed sources of history (newspapers, magazines, historical articles)
Identify major mountains in Cameroon (Mount Cameroon, Bamboutos Mountains) and locate them in immediate environments
Sing the National Anthem correctly, describe standing position for flag hoisting, and practice saying apologies

exercices.enonce: Fotso locates Mount Cameroon in Bafoussam: Mount Cameroon is the highest mountain in West/Central Africa. Apology: 'I am sorry.'
exercices.astuce: Mount Cameroon (4,040 m) is an active volcano in the South West Region.

quiz.question: Which mountain is the highest peak in Cameroon and West Africa?
quiz.explication: Mount Cameroon (4,040 m) is the highest peak.

quiz.question: Which of these is a written source of historical news and events?
quiz.explication: Newspapers record historical events in print.

quiz.question: What phrase promotes ethical values when you accidentally bump into a classmate?
quiz.explication: 'I am sorry' is a polite apology.

lecons.contenu:
Sources of History (Newspapers & Magazines), Physical Features (Mountains in Cameroon), National Anthem, and Apologies

What you will learn:

  • Describe printed sources of history (newspapers, magazines, historical articles)
  • Identify major mountains in Cameroon (Mount Cameroon, Bamboutos Mountains) and locate them in immediate environments
  • Sing the National Anthem correctly, describe standing position for flag hoisting, and practice saying apologies

In Bafoussam (Week 2, Page 67-68), Fotso describes historical sources (newspapers, magazines), identifies mountains in Cameroon (Mount Cameroon), sings the National Anthem, and practices saying apologies!

lecons.titre: Sources of History (Letters & Diaries), Physical Features (Hills), Administrative Rulers, and Children's Rights
savoirs_faire: Describe written personal sources of history (letters, personal diaries, family records)
Identify hills in Cameroon and locate places in immediate environments
Name and identify administrative rulers (Senior Divisional Officer SDO, Divisional Officer DO, Governor) and state children's rights

exercices.enonce: Fotso names administrative rulers in Bafoussam: The Governor heads the Region; SDO heads the Division. Children's right: Right to education.
exercices.astuce: Children have the right to education, health, protection, and a name.

quiz.question: Which of these is a fundamental right of every child in Cameroon?
options: Right to education and health care
quiz.explication: Education and health are fundamental children's rights.

quiz.question: Which administrative ruler represents the state at the Division level in Cameroon?
quiz.explication: SDOs head administrative divisions.

quiz.question: How do personal diaries serve as sources of history?
options: They record daily written accounts of personal experiences and historical events
quiz.explication: Diaries record written historical experiences.

lecons.contenu:
Sources of History (Letters & Diaries), Physical Features (Hills), Administrative Rulers, and Children's Rights

What you will learn:

  • Describe written personal sources of history (letters, personal diaries, family records)
  • Identify hills in Cameroon and locate places in immediate environments
  • Name and identify administrative rulers (Senior Divisional Officer SDO, Divisional Officer DO, Governor) and state children's rights

In Bafoussam (Week 3, Page 68-69), Fotso describes sources of history (letters, diaries), identifies hills in Cameroon, names administrative rulers (SDO, DO, Governor), and states children's rights!

lecons.titre: Sources of History (Government Documents), Physical Features (Valleys), and Integration & Remediation
savoirs_faire: Describe official sources of history from government documents (gazettes, decrees, census reports)
Identify valleys in Cameroon and locate places in immediate environments
Apply acquired knowledge, skills, and attitudes to daily life situations and complete integration activities

exercices.enonce: Fotso describes valleys in Bafoussam: A valley is low land between hills or mountains. Source: Government gazette.
exercices.astuce: Valleys lie between hills or mountains and often contain rivers.

quiz.question: What physical geographical feature is defined as low land lying between hills or mountains?
quiz.explication: Valleys are low lands between hills.

quiz.question: Which official written document serves as an authoritative source of history?
quiz.explication: Government gazettes provide official history.

quiz.question: Why is studying local history important for young citizens in Bafoussam?
options: It teaches how our community developed and builds patriotic identity
quiz.explication: History builds civic identity and community understanding.

lecons.contenu:
Sources of History (Government Documents), Physical Features (Valleys), and Integration & Remediation

What you will learn:

  • Describe official sources of history from government documents (gazettes, decrees, census reports)
  • Identify valleys in Cameroon and locate places in immediate environments
  • Apply acquired knowledge, skills, and attitudes to daily life situations and complete integration activities

In Bafoussam (Week 4, Page 69), Fotso describes sources of history from government documents, identifies valleys in Cameroon, and performs integration, assessment, and remediation to complete September social studies!

lecons.titre: Components of a Computer: Keyboard and Mouse
savoirs_faire: Identify and name the primary input components of a computer (Keyboard and Mouse)
Describe the specific role of the keyboard (typing text, numbers, symbols) and mouse (pointing, clicking, dragging)
Explain the importance of input devices in giving instructions to computers

exercices.enonce: Mbella uses input devices in Douala: Keyboard keys letters into screen; mouse moves pointer and clicks icons.
exercices.astuce: The keyboard and mouse are input devices that send user commands to the computer.

quiz.question: Which input device contains keys used to type letters, numbers, and text into a computer in Douala?
quiz.explication: Keyboards contain keys for typing text.

quiz.question: Which computer device is moved on a desk to control the cursor and click on screen items?
quiz.explication: The mouse controls the screen cursor.

quiz.question: What mouse action opens an item or selects a button on the computer screen?
quiz.explication: Clicking selects items on screen.

lecons.contenu:

lecons.contenu:
Terminer une histoire, dictionnaire bilingue, verbes être/avoir, marque du nombre

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Dire ce qu'on ressent
  • Terminer une histoire avec le dictionnaire bilingue
  • Conjuguer être et avoir au présent

À Yaoundé (Semaine 1, Page 63), Mballa définit la communication et exprime ses sensations !

lecons.titre: Se situer dans l'espace, lecture d'un texte ouvert, sons [IE]/[IT], imparfait de l'indicatif, révision des accords
savoirs_faire: Se situer dans l'espace et dire où l'on va et d'où l'on vient (je vais à/au, je viens de/du/de la)
Développer le goût de la lecture avec un texte ouvert et trouver les sons [IE] et [IT]
Conjuguer les verbes à l'imparfait de l'indicatif et réviser les accords des adjectifs qualificatifs

exercices.enonce: Dans les rues de Yaoundé, Mballa dit : 'Je vais au marché, je viens de l'école.' (localisation)
exercices.astuce: Je vais à/au + lieu ; je viens de/du + lieu de provenance.

quiz.question: Comment dit-on qu'on se rend au marché ?
quiz.explication: 'Je vais au marché' indique la destination.

quiz.question: Lequel contient le son [IT] ?
quiz.explication: 'Petit' contient le son [IT].

quiz.question: Que permettent les moyens de communication ?
quiz.explication: Les moyens de communication aident à échanger et se situer.

lecons.contenu:
Se situer dans l'espace, sons [IE]/[IT], imparfait, révision des accords

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Se situer dans l'espace
  • Lire un texte ouvert
  • Conjuguer à l'imparfait et réviser les accords des adjectifs

À Yaoundé (Semaine 2, Page 64), Mballa découvre les différents moyens de communication et se situe dans l'espace !

lecons.titre: Les activités des hommes de la localité, verbes du deuxième groupe, et évaluation finale de fin d'année
savoirs_faire: Identifier les activités des hommes de sa localité (cultivateur, commerçant, forgeron, couturier)
Regrouper des mots par famille et conjuguer les verbes du deuxième groupe (finir, punir, sentir) au présent de l'indicatif
Écrire les nombres correctement ; réviser les outils traditionnels et modernes de communication pour l'évaluation finale de fin d'année

exercices.enonce: Au marché de Yaoundé, Mballa observe : 'Le forgeron finit son travail. Le couturier choisit son tissu.' (verbes du 2e groupe : finit, choisit)
exercices.astuce: Les verbes du deuxième groupe se conjuguent en -is, -is, -it au présent (je finis, tu finis, il finit).

quiz.question: Quel métier travaille le fer ?
quiz.explication: Le forgeron travaille le fer.

quiz.question: 'Finir' est un verbe de quel groupe ?
quiz.explication: 'Finir' se conjugue comme les verbes du deuxième groupe.

quiz.question: Que révise-t-on lors de l'évaluation de fin d'année ?
options: Toute l'année, dont les outils de communication
quiz.explication: L'évaluation finale couvre l'ensemble de l'année scolaire, avec un accent sur avril.

lecons.contenu:
Activités des hommes de la localité, verbes du deuxième groupe, évaluation finale de fin d'année

Ce que tu vas apprendre :

  • Identifier les activités des hommes de sa localité
  • Conjuguer les verbes du deuxième groupe
  • Réviser les outils de communication pour l'évaluation finale

À Yaoundé (Semaines 3-4, Pages 65-66), Mballa découvre les outils traditionnels et modernes de communication, et révise toute l'année pour l'évaluation finale !
